title: Perfect ring complexes are closed under triangle extensions
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $C_1\to C_2\to C_3\to C_1[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in the derived category $D(A)$ of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $C_1$ and $C_3$ are perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], meaning isomorphic in $D(A)$ to bounded complexes of finitely generated projective $A$-modules, then $C_2$ is perfect.

source.place: Tag 066R, lemma-two-out-of-three-perfect, the first-and-third-imply-second case; also WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/Perfect.lean:215-243, DerivedCategory.isPerfect_obj₂_of_distTriang.

proof.text: Write the given triangle as $T=(C_1\xrightarrow{u}C_2\xrightarrow{v}C_3\xrightarrow{\delta}C_1[1])$. By [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], choose bounded complexes $P_1,P_3$ of finitely generated projective $A$-modules and isomorphisms $e_1:Q(P_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_1$ and $e_3:Q(P_3)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_3$. Choose bounds $a_j\le b_j$ such that $P_j^i=0$ outside $[a_j,b_j]$ for $j=1,3$; zero complexes permit any bounds. The complex $P_1[1]$ has term $P_1^{i+1}$, differential $-d_{P_1}$, and bounds $[a_1-1,b_1-1]$. By the commutation of $Q$ with shifts in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $e_1$ induces an isomorphism $s:Q(P_1[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}C_1[1]$. Keep the chosen localization universe of $D(A)$ throughout; no equality with the universe of module carriers is assumed.

source.place: Tag 066R, lemma-two-out-of-three-perfect, first/third case; direct bounded-projective cone argument, setup (agent proof).

proof.text: Form $g=s^{-1}\circ\delta\circ e_3:Q(P_3)\to Q(P_1[1])$. Apply [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] to the abelian category of $A$-modules, the source $P_3$, and the target complex $P_1[1]$. The source is bounded above by $b_3$ and all its terms are projective. Surjectivity of the stated bijection gives a homotopy class of chain maps; choose a representative $f:P_3\to P_1[1]$. By definition of the canonical map from the homotopy category to the derived category, $Q(f)=g$, equivalently $s\circ Q(f)=\delta\circ e_3$. The lemma places no bound or projectivity restriction on its target and works in the specified localization universe.

source.place: Tag 064B, lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex; bounded-above projective Hom bijection used in the agent direct cone proof of the first/third case of Tag 066R, lemma-two-out-of-three-perfect.

proof.text: Let $F=C(f)$ be the actual mapping cone of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Explicitly $F^i=P_1^{i+1}\oplus P_3^{i+1}$ and $d_F^i(y,x)=(-d_{P_1}^{i+1}y+f^{i+1}x,-d_{P_3}^{i+1}x)$. It is zero outside $[L,U]$, where $L=\min(a_1-1,a_3-1)$ and $U=\max(b_1-1,b_3-1)$. Each term is finitely generated: if $(y_r)$ and $(x_t)$ generate the two summands, then $(y_r,0)$ and $(0,x_t)$ generate their sum. Each term is projective by the lifting characterization of [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]: given a surjection and a map from the sum, lift its restrictions to the two projective summands and add the two lifts. Thus $F$ is a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules, without any Noetherian hypothesis. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its cone triangle $Q(P_3)\xrightarrow{Q(f)}Q(P_1[1])\to Q(F)\to Q(P_3)[1]$ is distinguished.

source.place: Tag 066R, lemma-two-out-of-three-perfect; explicit cone calculation using derived-category cone convention (agent proof).

proof.text: Twice rotate $T$ using (TR2) of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The resulting distinguished triangle has vertices $C_3,C_1[1],C_2[1]$ and arrows $\delta,-u[1],-v[1]$. The equality $s\circ Q(f)=\delta\circ e_3$ of Step 2 supplies the commuting first square from the distinguished cone triangle of Step 3 to this twice-rotated triangle. By (TR3) of [def-weil-triangulated-category], extend $(e_3,s)$ to a morphism of these triangles, with third component $c:Q(F)\to C_2[1]$. Both $e_3$ and $s$ are isomorphisms, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $c$ an isomorphism. This proves $Q(F)\cong C_2[1]$, rather than assuming that an unspecified derived arrow already has a finite-projective cone.

source.place: Tag 066R, lemma-two-out-of-three-perfect, direct first/third cone argument; TR2/TR3 and two-isomorphisms triangle comparison.

proof.text: Shift the isomorphism of Step 4 by $[-1]$. Since $Q$ commutes with shifts [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], compose it with $Q(F[-1])\cong Q(F)[-1]$ and the cancellation isomorphism $(C_2[1])[-1]\cong C_2$ to obtain $Q(F[-1])\cong C_2$. The term in degree $i$ of $F[-1]$ is $F^{i-1}$, its differential is $-d_F$, and it is zero outside $[L+1,U+1]$. Its terms are precisely the finitely generated projective modules of Step 3 with reindexed degrees. Thus $F[-1]$ and the displayed isomorphism are the bounded finite-projective model required by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]; $C_2$ is perfect.
